# Question: generator shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut that fits every canonical demonstration is:

> Count every distinct color, including zero, then subtract one; upscale by that
> factor.

Every canonical input contains zero, so this shortcut agrees there with the
intended count of distinct nonzero colors.

An exact disagreement input emitted by the repaired production sampler is:

```json
[[1, 9, 5], [5, 1, 9], [9, 5, 1]]
```

This is seed `0`, sample index `1`, difficulty `medium`, with
`color_count=3` and `zero_present=false`. The intended rule upscales by 3 and
produces a 9×9 output. The shortcut computes `3 - 1 = 2` and produces a 6×6
output. I checked the intended output through the selected canonical Racket
runtime, not only the Python mirror; the source-bound receipt is
`checks/question/generator-shortcuts/racket-final.json`, and the rival output is
`checks/question/generator-shortcuts/rival_output.json`.

Yes, the generator emits such cases by design. Two positions in each five-item
schedule are zero-free, and the retained witness is also stored at
`repo/generators/4ca8a7b38652/counterexamples/always_subtract_one.json`.
